newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania rejects claims of poor coffee quality.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania rejects claims of poor coffee quality.

text.p: Industry officials and traders in Tanzania have strongly rejected claims that Tanzanian coffee quality is declining.
The managing director of the Tanzania Coffee Board, Edward Sannda, told Reuters on Wednesday that while production was down, quality was clearly up.
"For the quality, it is the best since the liberalisation programme was started (in 1993)," Sannda told Reuters.
Board spokesman Damian Salla said media reports from Kenya this week claiming that Tanzanian coffee was suffering quality problems were "totally false and without foundation".
Salla cited one newspaper quoting unnamed Tanzanian farmers as saying local Tanzanian coffee quality was declining.
He said the coffee board had nothing to hide as the official Tanzanian body representing the coffee industry and it would welcome any inquiries regarding any quality issues.
"Quality is not going down; it's improving a little bit," said Jeremy Lefroy, managing director of Africa Coffee Co.
Further evidence that quality was not falling was the "relatively good" price Tanzania was getting for its coffee on the world market, said Lefroy.
Nitesh Virji of Universal Export-Import Group (Uneximp), a major Moshi-based coffee trading house, agreed.
"The board is 100 percent conscious of quality and quantity at the moment," he said.
